amendment.text: Knoxville does not amend the toilet-count table, the half-and-half split, rounding, the urinal rule, the small-occupancy exceptions or the single-user and all-gender provisions. Its only change to the toilet rules is to set out the text of plumbing code Section 403.3.3 and building code Section 2902.3.3 (where toilets are located): not more than one story above or below the space served and a path of travel of not more than 500 feet, with exceptions for factory and industrial employees and for storage occupancies where approved. Knoxville is on the 2024 edition while the state is on 2021; the office, restaurant and school ratios, the 50/50 split, rounding up and the 50% and 67% urinal limits read the same in both. Differences in the 2024 text: the urinal limit is a share of the water closets required 'for males', and a shared all-gender room needs water closet compartments (405.3.4) and urinal partitions (405.3.5).
amendment.quote: Amend Chapter 4, Fixtures, Faucets and Fixture Fittings, as follows: Amend the text of Section 403.3.3 Location of toilet facilities in occupancies other than malls. In occupancies other than covered and open mall buildings, the required public and employee toilet facilities shall be located not more than one story above or below the space required to be provided with toilet facilities, and the path of travel to such facilities shall not exceed a distance of 500 feet (152 m).
amendment.note: Whether this text differs from the unamended 2024 model section was not compared (the model text was not opened separately).

quotes.small_occupancy: Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. quotes.urinal_partitions: Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy. The horizontal dimension between walls or partitions at each urinal shall be not less than 30 inches (762 mm). The walls or partitions shall begin at a height not greater than 12 inches (305 mm) from and extend not less than 60 inches (1524 mm) above the finished floor surface.

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 25 / 25 = 1 each. Urinals may replace at most 50% of 1 = 0.5, so 0.
50 each. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2. Urinals: 50% of 2 = 1.
100 each. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 50 at 1 per 50 = 1, total 3. Urinals: 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 each. First 50 = 2, remaining 150 at 1 per 50 = 3, total 5. Urinals: 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 each. 25 / 75 = 0.33, rounded up to 1. Urinals: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so 0.
100 each. 100 / 75 = 1.33, rounded up to 2. Urinals: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200 / 75 = 2.67, rounded up to 3. Urinals: 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Same results as the state pack and Nashville: the 2024 ratios Knoxville enforces equal the 2021 ratios. Urinals are optional; the code does not say how the 50% and 67% limits round, and the examples round down.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Knoxville job sites. Price your restroom, pick the right material and see the City of Knoxville rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Knoxville offices, restaurants, university buildings and hospitals, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Tennessee law uses the federal access standards as its own for public buildings. Knoxville's building rules also apply a national accessibility standard, in its 2017 edition, and the plans are approved by the office that reviews the project.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Knoxville's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Knoxville sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Tennessee and federal stall rules match:** Tennessee adopted the federal standards word for word, so a stall, door or grab bar that meets one meets the other. The 2017 standard in Knoxville's building rules is a separate document, so ask Knoxville Plans Review and Inspections which sizes it checks on your project.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** under Knoxville's rules a one-person restroom is marked as open to everyone. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and every urinal has privacy partitions. Since July 2026, state law requires shared restrooms in public colleges and universities, state prisons, juvenile detention facilities and domestic violence shelters to be designated for females, males or families. A 2021 law covers shared restrooms in public schools.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Knoxville requires a permit to alter or repair a building. Its list of work that needs no building permit includes painting, tiling, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work, and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high. It doesn't name toilet partitions. The city issues a commercial repair permit for like-for-like work and a commercial alteration permit for changes to appearance or function. Ask Knoxville Plans Review and Inspections (865-215-4311) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: Knoxville counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and every toilet needs a stall with a door. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, each with a privacy screen. The table shows toilets only.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. An office for 25 people or fewer, or any space for 15 or fewer, may use one shared room. Knoxville's ordinance also says where the toilets go: no more than one floor above or below the space they serve, and no more than 500 feet away along the route people walk.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or Knoxville Plans Review and Inspections sets the final number.
skip_state_sources: Toilet counts under the state code
Fire test for solid plastic partitions: 2021
page.install_rule: Knoxville requires anyone who applies for a permit to hold a city registration matched to their qualifications, sometimes alongside a Tennessee state license. Tennessee requires a state contractor license to bid or take commercial projects of $25,000 or more. Confirm what your project needs with Knoxville Plans Review and Inspections. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who applies for a Knoxville permit needs a city registration.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Tennessee's wage law for public work covers state highway projects only, so on a school or city building a set wage applies only where federal money brings in the federal wage rules. The federal rate for a carpenter on building work in Knox County is $20.09 an hour, with no benefits amount listed.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 9.25% in Knoxville: 7% state and 2.25% local. In most of Tennessee the local part applies only to the first $1,600 of the price of each single item, and the state adds 2.75% on the part of an item's price between $1,600 and $3,200.
page.buyers_extra: - **University and college buildings:** HDPE or phenolic for restrooms that take heavy student traffic and frequent cleaning.
